editorial.marketOverview: Nasdaq and semiconductor leadership entered the holiday-shortened week under heavy selling pressure. Friday's Nasdaq Composite -5.28%, QQQ -5.67% and SOX roughly -10.7% are reported historical observations, not Sunday live quotes. Sector underperformance and weak breadth favor downside continuation until a sustained reversal is observed.
editorial.whatChanged: No verified new US cash-session response has occurred since the previous assessment. Reuters November 22 and the latest calendar confirm correction-versus-rebound uncertainty and a concentrated three-session catalyst calendar. The curated Open Watch feed has no update after November 21 00:44 UTC. These calendar details sharpen event timing, not directional conviction.
editorial.marketInterpretation: An oversold rebound is plausible following outsized semiconductor liquidation, but cannot be treated as a trend reversal without QQQ/SOX relative-strength recovery, expanding participation and easing volatility. Friday VIX reporting is inconsistent between 35.89 and 37.66; no synchronized VXN observation is available. The historical 10Y–2Y spread of 29 basis points was computed as 4.94% minus 4.65%, multiplied by 100 basis points per percentage point; inputs are stale and not a current curve reading. Friday Brent and WTI settlements are historical, contract maturity not independently matched; FedWatch probabilities unavailable.
editorial.threeDayPath: Monday November 23: monitor flash PMI and opening breadth for a capitulation rebound or renewed liquidation. Tuesday November 24: consumer confidence and semiconductor/AI hardware earnings expectations may amplify volatility; Dell's results are expected after close. Wednesday November 25: PCE and GDP create the most direct rates-driven repricing risk, with Beige Book later; holiday-shortened liquidity can magnify moves. Directional baseline remains bearish with elevated two-way volatility, not a deterministic daily forecast.
editorial.bullCase: A durable bounce would require semiconductor participation rather than QQQ gains driven by a few defensives, with positive breadth, falling VXN/VIX and stable or declining yields. Favorable PMI, earnings guidance or PCE could provide a catalyst, but their outcomes are unknown.
editorial.bearCase: Continued SOX weakness, adverse AI financing or regulatory headlines, sticky inflation, rising yields, or energy escalation could compound Friday's liquidation. Elevated fear alone does not guarantee a bottom.
editorial.watchNext: Verify Monday opening QQQ, SOX/SMH and breadth on matched timestamps; obtain primary VXN/VIX and Treasury 2Y/10Y pairs, current contract-specific Brent/WTI and CME FedWatch; reconcile Friday VIX discrepancies; monitor new curated Open Watch events and official macro releases before changing bias.
